response.rationale: R3 is the strongest candidate because the lesion is vascular/malignant by CD31-positive vascular channels, perivascular proliferation, and mitoses/necrosis. R1 is directly contradicted by negative Kaposi sarcoma–associated herpesvirus staining, and R4 relies only on the patient's prior squamous cell carcinoma history without supportive squamous histology.

rejected.why: Negative staining for Kaposi sarcoma–associated herpesvirus directly contradicts Kaposi sarcoma, and no supportive raw spans were provided.
Only the prior history of squamous cell carcinomas supports R4; the hematoxylin-eosin findings of ovoid perivascular tumor cells and vascular markers do not support squamous differentiation.
